decision.reason_for: An early direct Hebrew numeral converges with the Greek tradition and an ancient retelling. This is more than a two-copy contrast.
decision.counterargument: Six is also ancient, as versional evidence shows. An intentional reduction of six remains possible; manuscript age cannot rule it out.
decision.transmission_explanation: Assimilation of the numeral to nearby six hundred is plausible, not demonstrated. A simpler number is not automatically earlier.
decision.chronological_effect: Modest advantage to the early Hebrew attestation of four. Do not date the six reading only to Leningrad.
decision.independence_effect: Greek tradition and Josephus are related evidence, not three or four independent Hebrew votes.
decision.publication_action: Record four as the working critical choice and retain six in the apparatus; canonical files remain unchanged in this research pass.
open_questions: Verify consequential manuscript assignments against an apparatus or page image before promotion.
Determine whether a broader Samuel literary-form policy changes the target text.
excluded_evidence: Conflicting summaries of Alexandrinus were not used to break the tie.
Five-cubit reports were not fully collated and are not adjudicated in this pilot.
decision.summary: Prefer four, retaining six as a material variant.

decision.reason_for: Direct Qumran Hebrew and an early Greek strand converge on a divine referent; the following verse about Israel as Yahweh's portion coheres with that reading.
decision.counterargument: The Samaritan Hebrew tradition and Peshitta join MT on Israel. The symbolism of the nations and Israel supplies a contextual explanation for that reading.
decision.transmission_explanation: A change of referent in transmission is plausible. This pilot does not assert a particular scribe's theological motive or exclude every alternative history.
decision.chronological_effect: Older direct and versional attestations modestly favor God; later copies do not establish that Israel itself originated late.
decision.independence_effect: Greek sons and angels readings are related versional support, not separate complete Hebrew witnesses.
decision.publication_action: Use sons of God as the working English alternative. Preserve sons of Israel and distinguish angels as Greek interpretation. No canonical source rewrite in this pass.
open_questions: Verify image-level surviving versus supplied letters and spelling before claiming a new diplomatic transcription.
Audit additional Qumran fragment coverage rather than treating every Deuteronomy fragment as supporting this verse.
Prefer the divine referent without claiming that Greek can distinguish an earlier El wording from Elohim; the displayed Hebrew follows the documented Qumran form.
excluded_evidence: No reconstructed sons of El reading is asserted as the uniquely recovered autograph.
decision.summary: Prefer a divine referent (sons of God); the exact earlier Hebrew form remains open.

decision.reason_for: A Hebrew scroll and multiple ancient versional streams attest a nun line, fitting the acrostic sequence.
decision.counterargument: The Qumran form contains other expansion. The line could complete an acrostic, and its second half resembles verse 17. Omission is also ancient.
decision.transmission_explanation: Both loss and acrostic repair are plausible. Inclusion is the present working preference, not an assertion that the Qumran wording is the exact original.
decision.chronological_effect: Early Hebrew presence matters, but early omission and uncertain relationships prevent age from deciding exact wording.
decision.independence_effect: The Gallican Psalter does not add an independent Hebrew vote beyond Greek. The medieval margin has uncertain derivation.
decision.publication_action: Retain a separate line-presence decision and display Qumran wording as a labeled witness alternative. Hold exact-wording promotion.
open_questions: God versus Yahweh/Lord is not resolved as the earliest divine designation.
All his words versus his words differs across witnesses.
Check the argument for secondary acrostic repair and the relation to verse 17 before final adoption.
excluded_evidence: No single Latin Vulgate vote: Greek-based and Hebrew-based Psalters differ.
decision.summary: Tentatively include a nun line; do not yet select its exact wording.
